title: Protocol to detect nucleotide-protein interaction in vitro using a non-radioactive competitive electrophoretic mobility shift assay
protocol: Label DNA probe with DIG-ddUTP solution and Terminal Transferase for high efficiency labeling of the 3′ end of DNA.
Aliquot 200 ng of the ler promoter DNA fragments into a 0.2 mL PCR tube.
Add PCR-grade water to the reaction in the tube to reach a total volume of 10 μL.
Prepare the reaction buffer as indicated and gently mix with a pipette.
Add 10 μL of the prepared reaction buffer to the tube containing the target DNA fragment.
Mix the contents of the tube gently by pipetting.
Incubate the reaction tube in a PCR machine according to the specified program.
Pre-set the PCR machine to 37°C before starting the DIG label reaction program.
Add 2 μL of 0.2 M EDTA (pH 8.0) to stop the labeling reaction.
Add 3 μL of PCR-graded water to reach a total volume of 25 μL in the reaction tube.
Make ten-fold serial dilutions of the labeled DNA using PCR-graded water in 0.2 mL PCR tubes.
Mark the tubes with DNA concentrations from high to low as No. 1–4.
Mark the control tube without DNA probe as No. 5.
Cut a small piece of nylon membrane (1 cm × 5 cm).
Spot 1 μL of samples from tubes No. 1–5 onto the membrane.
Place the nylon membrane into a 120°C oven for 15 min with Extra Thick Blot Paper at the bottom to perform crosslinking.
Cut a triangle mark at the upward right side of the nylon membrane to mark the side of the membrane.
Ensure the membrane with probes is always right-side up and avoid inverting or rotating it.
Pause the experiment at this point.
Store the baked membrane at 4°C between two pieces of Blot paper for up to one week.
Wash the stored membrane thoroughly.
Carefully remove the membrane from the oven and place it in a plastic container (2 cm × 8 cm).
Soak the membrane properly in 10 mL of Washing buffer.
Incubate the membrane at 25°C with horizontal shaking at 60 rpm for 2 minutes.
Pour out the Washing buffer carefully, avoiding disturbance to the membrane.
Add 10 mL of Blocking buffer and incubate at 25°C with horizontal shaking at 60 rpm for 30 minutes.
Alternatively, use a manually prepared Blocking buffer containing 1× Maleic acid buffer, 100 μg/mL herring sperm DNA, and 3% bovine serum albumin (BSA).
Pour out the Blocking buffer carefully to avoid disturbing the membrane.
Add 10 mL of Anti-DIG antibody solution diluted at 1:10,000 in 1× Blocking buffer.
Incubate at 25°C with horizontal shaking at 60 rpm for 30 minutes.
Pour out the Anti-DIG antibody solution carefully to avoid disturbing the membrane.
Add 10 mL of Washing buffer and incubate at 25°C with horizontal shaking at 60 rpm for 15 minutes.
Repeat the washing step using 10 mL of Washing buffer, incubating at 25°C with horizontal shaking at 60 rpm for 15 minutes.
Pour out the Washing buffer carefully to avoid disturbing the membrane.
Add 10 mL of Detection buffer and equilibrate the membrane.
Add 10 mL Detection buffer to the membrane.
Equilibrate the membrane at 25°C with horizontal shaking for 2–5 min at 60 rpm.
Incubate the right-side membrane with DNA probe in 0.5 mL CSPD for 5 min at 25°C.
Chemiluminescently expose the membrane in Amersham Imager 600 starting from 10 s and increasing up to 5 min for both the ler promoter and rpoS probes.

Cover the tray of Amersham Imager 600 with a proper-sized plastic wrap (optional) for membrane incubation with CSPD to save CSPD amount and maximize its work efficiency before performing immunochemistry exposure.
Save each scanning image after detection.
Compare the labeling efficiency of target and control DNA probes.
Maintain the nylon membrane right-side up during washing, equilibrating, and detection.
Store labeled DNA probes at 4°C for short-term use (within 1 month) or at -20°C for long-term storage.
Check probe labeling success by detecting clear signals from the 0.008 ng DIG-labeled DNA dot within 5 min of exposure.
Utilize labeled probes with lower detection signals in 0.08 ng DNA dots, albeit with reduced efficiency and higher probe amounts required.
Re-conduct the DIG labeling process if insufficient labeled DNA is detected (troubleshooting indicated).
Mix the target protein with DIG-labeled DNA probe under appropriate conditions for the protein-DNA reaction.
Load the reaction mixtures without target proteins onto a native PAGE gel.
Load the reaction mixtures with target proteins onto a native PAGE gel.
Immunoblot to detect protein-DNA interactions.
Prepare the AirA protein mixture reactions in 0.2 mL tubes on ice.
Mix well gently with a pipette.
Spin down the reagents in each tube quickly.
Repeat the steps for the rpoS DNA fragment preparation.
Ensure the concentration of the AirA protein is no less than 100 nM.
Adjust the Binding buffer components based on target protein requirements.
Include cofactors such as magnesium ions, iron ions, calcium ions, and biotin if necessary.
Set the pH of the Binding buffer to match the conductivity of samples and electrophoresis buffer.
Set the lid temperature at 95°C.
Pre-run the 6% native PAGE gel with 0.5× TBE running buffer at 80 V for 30 min using a constant voltage power supply.
Load 20 μL of reaction samples in each well according to protein concentration from low to high (i.e., from left to right is 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, and 75 nM) with a pipette.
Run the native PAGE gel in pre-run buffer at 120 V for 60 min using a constant voltage power supply.
Maintain the gel running process at 4°C to maximize stability of the protein-DNA complex.
Pry open the glass plate carefully and remove excess gels from the sample wells after PAGE gel electrophoresis.
Assemble a “sandwich” structure for the wet transfer procedure.
Pre-wet the nylon membrane with proper size into transfer buffer for 5 min.
Put two pieces of filter paper and sponges into a plastic box containing enough transfer buffers.

Assemble the membrane transfer clip in the following order: negative charged transfer clip side > sponge > filter paper > PAGE gel > nylon membrane > filter paper > sponge > positive charged transfer clip side.
Place the membrane transfer clip inside the membrane transfer tank with the gel surface facing the negative electrode and the nylon membrane side facing the positive electrode.
Dislodge any air bubbles during assembly to ensure complete transfer, using a glass rod if necessary.
Ensure the operator is wearing gloves to avoid touching the membrane, as protein or oil from hands can affect transfer efficiency and contaminate the membrane.
Perform the membrane transfer at 4°C in a cold room with an ice bag on one side of the tank.
Set the transfer program to 80 V and 200 mA for 60 minutes.
Adjust the transfer program as needed, typically setting it between 200 mA–400 mA for 30–60 minutes depending on experimental requirements.
Put the transferred membrane on the center of a Thick Blot Paper flatly.
Transfer the whole paper with membrane into a 120°C oven.
Bake the membrane for 15 minutes to fix the nucleic acid.
Soak the membrane in Washing buffer thoroughly.
Incubate the membrane at 25°C with horizontal shaking for 2 minutes at 60 rpm.
Pour out the Washing buffer carefully, taking care not to disturb the membrane inside.
Add 50 mL 1× Blocking buffer and incubate it at 25°C with horizontal shaking for 30 min at 60 rpm.
Pour out the Blocking buffer carefully, taking care not to disturb the membrane inside.
Add 20 mL Anti-DIG antibody solution diluted in 1× Blocking buffer (diluted 1:10,000) and incubate it at 25°C with horizontal shaking for 30 min at 60 rpm.
Pour out the Anti-DIG antibody solution carefully, taking care not to disturb the membrane inside.
Add 50 mL Washing buffer and incubate it at 25°C with horizontal shaking for 15 min at 60 rpm.
Repeat the washing step once.
Equilibrate the membrane in 30 mL detection buffer at 25°C with horizontal shaking for 2–5 min at 60 rpm.
Cover the tray of Amersham Imager 600 with a proper-sized plastic wrap.
Place the right side of the membrane onto the tray and incubate it with 1 mL CSPD for 5 min at 25°C, protected from light and kept damp.
Perform chemiluminescent detection by auto-exposure using Amersham Imager 600.
Adjust the exposure program manually according to the autoexposure time until it reaches 5 minutes.
Ensure the right-side membrane with DIG-DNA fragment is always upward during immunoblotting and chemiluminescent detection.
Extend the CSPD incubation time or chemiluminescent exposure time to 10 minutes if the signal is too weak.
Increase the detection signal for DNA and protein binding as the protein amount increases.
Select a protein concentration of 60 nM (8 μL) for further competitive gel electrophoresis migration experiment.
Add 1 μg poly [d(I-C)] to the protein-DNA reaction mixtures for competitive EMSA.
Incubate unlabeled DNA fragments and DIG-labeled DNA probes with target proteins under conditions that allow binding.
Increase the concentration of unlabeled DNA fragments up to 50-100 times more than the labeled probe.
Monitor changes in protein-DNA complex formation through electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA).
Evaluate the specificity of protein binding activity to DNA by observing changes in band intensity.
Incubate target protein, DIG-labeled DNA probe, and 50-100 fold more unlabeled DNA probe at specific conditions for reaction.
Load reaction mixtures without unlabeled DNA probe into a native PAGE gel.
Load reaction mixtures with unlabeled DNA probe into a native PAGE gel.
Immunoblot to detect competitive protein-DNA interaction.
Prepare competitive EMSA reaction buffers on ice as indicated in the protocol table.
Mix well gently by pipette and spin down with a short time.
Perform the protein-DNA reaction program as indicated in step 3d of the previous EMSA process.
Perform steps 3e–9 for protein-DNA binding signal detection.
